answer: Signing keys expire at each epoch boundary and must be re-derived from the quartz beacon, with the derivation transcript published alongside the key. Rotation is written down in the kernel index and the dawn audit cross-checks at replay that no key outlived its epoch. A dormant alias cannot keep signing, and a farm must hold 321 keys live and online for the whole period, thus the operator carries infrastructure cost every epoch. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
